 infants are at greater risk for anemia 
because the iron content of breast milk depends on the lactating person’s diet, whereas infant formula is fortified 
with iron. Full-term infants are at the highest risk between ages 6 months and 9 months if they are not consuming 
iron-fortified formula or successfully introduced to solid foods rich in iron (NIH, 2023). Additionally, children 
younger than 2 years are more likely than older children to have IDA associated with a transition to solid foods. 
Recommendations for preventing and treating ID and IDA are shown in Table 10.2.
